name: Citizenship by Relevant Investment

qualifying_event.description: A foreign national who makes an investment the Ministry of Economy deems 'relevant' may apply for Argentine citizenship through a dedicated agency, bypassing the standard 2-year residence requirement.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Documented investment; application to the Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión; security-clearance review; National Migration Directorate approval.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires an investment certified as 'relevant' by the Ministry of Economy -- the Ministry alone defines what qualifies, and no fixed public minimum investment amount or qualifying investment-type list had been published as of this research pass.
The Agency obtains clearance reports on the applicant from the Security Ministry, the Financial Intelligence Unit, and intelligence agencies before issuing a recommendation.

sources.title: República Argentina -- Ley 346 de Ciudadanía y Naturalización (texto actualizado), Artículo 2: naturalization via 'una inversión relevante en el país' as certified by the Ministry of Economy, alongside the standard 2-year residence route

Argentina.gob.ar official announcement -- Investment Citizenship Programs Agency (under the Ministry of Economy): process (application, Agency evaluation, security-clearance checks, recommendation to National Migration Directorate, 30 business days to decide); legal basis Decree 524/2025 amending Decree 366/25 and Ley 346

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Argentina). BRAND NEW PROGRAM, worth flagging prominently: this is described by multiple secondary sources as South America's first formal Citizenship-by-Investment program, created via Decree 524/2025 amending Ley 346, with an implementing Agency (Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión) further formalized by Decree 285/2026 (Boletín Oficial, published 2026-04-28). The legal existence, administering agency, and process steps are all tier-1 confirmed directly on argentina.gob.ar. HOWEVER, as of this research pass, no public minimum investment threshold or defined list of qualifying investment types had been published -- the Ministry of Economy is empowered to determine 'relevant investment' but the announcement itself states this was still pending definition. This is genuinely different from every other CBI-style route in this dataset (Caribbean nations all publish a specific dollar figure per fund/option) -- modeled the requirement as existence-only (hard:true) without a threshold, rather than inventing or guessing a number. Revisit this file once a concrete threshold is published in the Boletín Oficial or a Ministry of Economy resolution.
